$comment: U54 -- SW1-SW4 are on the wrong land pattern. Review item 37, which the
review filed under 'simplification' as 'one part on two land patterns'. It
is not a tidiness issue; it is a fit defect.
All six buttons are the same part, C5340169 (hanxia HX TS4538CJ 250gf 009),
on two different footprints:
Both agree on the 3.00 mm row pitch (pads at y +/-1.500) and both drill
1.0 mm. They disagree by 0.4 mm of lead span, and the part has exactly one
true span, so one of them is wrong.
SETTLED FROM THE VENDOR DRAWING, not by inference. The datasheet's
recommended PCB pattern (LCSC 2212291730_hanxia-HX-TS4538CJ-250gf-009) is
dimensioned 5 mm horizontally, 3 mm vertically, holes ø1. That is the LS5.0
footprint exactly. SW6/SW7 are correct; SW1-SW4 are 0.2 mm out per side.
Reading it needed a rasteriser: the drawing is vector, the only embedded
image on the page is the vendor logo, and the dimension callouts do not
survive text extraction. pymupdf renders it; poppler is not installed and
needs a sudo password.
WHY THIS IS A FIT DEFECT AND NOT A MARGIN. The same drawing specifies the
leads as 4-ø0.95±0.1 into ø1.0 holes -- 0.025 mm of radial slack at nominal,
and none at all at the +0.1 lead tolerance. There is nothing to absorb a
0.2 mm per-side error with. SW1-SW4 would not seat without splaying the
leads, and these are hand-soldered, so it would have been discovered with a
part in one hand and an iron in the other.
THE FIX IS A FOOTPRINT SWAP, NOT A MOVE. Position, rotation, side, reference,
value and attributes are all preserved; only the land pattern changes, and
every pad's net is carried across BY PAD NUMBER (KTD27 -- never by order).
The correct footprint already exists in the same library, so nothing new is
added and no part number changes: the BOM is untouched.
ROUTING SURVIVES, and that is worth stating because U11's telltale swap had
to be reverted over exactly this. Only pad1 (/BTNn_SW) and pad4 (/GND) are
connected on these four; pads 2 and 3 are unconnected. The pads move 0.2 mm
and the pads are 1.6 mm square, so an existing track ending at the old centre
is still 0.6 mm inside the new pad. Nothing needs re-laying.
Both pads move INWARD, which also relaxes review item 33 slightly -- SW1-SW4
sit 0.45 mm from R28-R31 courtyard-to-courtyard, and this buys 0.2 mm of it
back.
The schematic's Footprint field for these four is updated to match in the
same change. That is the half a board-only edit would miss, and
--schematic-parity is the only check that compares a footprint to its SYMBOL.

steps.step: 1/1  SW1-SW4 onto the datasheet's 5.0 x 3.0 land pattern
